what: Wording this site changes on specific imported pages when sync_newsroom.py imports the newsroom, so it holds on newsroom.sgit.ai and not on sgit.ai. Each is a recorded rule and not a hand edit: validate.js check 11 still passes because the import writes the page. The import stops, loudly, if the text a rule replaces is not in its page exactly once, which means sgit.ai changed it and the rule is stale. When sgit.ai adopts the wording, delete the rule here. A rule has a separate match for the HTML page and its markdown twin.

find.html: Kept in this browser, and only here. The balance, the history and the receipts are in this browser's storage; nothing is sent anywhere and there is no account. A new browser, a private window or clearing site data starts again with £5.00 and no history, so with no personalisation. It never blocks a page and it never nags: credit can go below zero, the balance says so in the top bar, and that is all. How the meter works, and why we run it this way.

**Where your data is kept.** Your balance, history and receipts are kept in this browser’s storage, and your reading is not sent anywhere unless you choose to send it. There is no account. This is a client-side application: the pages are static files, with no server of ours behind them for now, and if encrypted vaults are added this page will say so. A new browser, a private window or clearing site data starts again with £5.00 and no history. Credit can go below zero, and no page is blocked.

What can leave your browser, when you choose to, is a payment (made on Stripe’s own page), a subscription or a reading share: [what leaves your browser, and when](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/shipped/index.html#data). [How the meter works](../meter/index.md), and [why it works this way](../articles/going-live-with-the-reading-meter.md).

overrides.why: The note said "nothing is sent anywhere", which is about the reading data and reads as wider than that once a top-up link exists, and it was written in a chatty register ("it never nags", "and that is all") on a page that now takes payment. It now says what is kept where, what can leave the browser and when, in plain terms and without absolutes.
